outcome_unknown_note: Hints of kind outcome_unknown (delegated host-work I.4.6): the body's type is atem-push-hint and its label atem-push-hint-v1 like an approval hint's, told apart by `kind` (no `state`, no session_id, process_gen or approval_id; `alert_id` instead). The task, session, sender and reason are only in the sealed part, jcs of {reason, sender, session_id, task_id}. info = enc(["atem-push-seal-v1", account_id, genesis_hash, host_id, u64(host_trust_gen), "outcome_unknown", alert_id, u64(created_at), u64(expires_at), device_id, enc_kid]) (11 fields; an approval's has 12). ikmE_hex = SHA-256(enc(["atem-r9-test-ikm", ikm_label])). Entries 0 and 1 are one alert for two recipients; entry 2 is another alert at the bounds. Only a delegated sender's (member:, service: or host:) UUID v4 task raises an alert. outcome_unknown_acks are the push_ack entries, one per hint. Each outcome_unknown_invalid carries the first hint's sealed envelope (except bad_sealed's, which is the point) so only its code refuses it; the runner checks the code with both verifiers. Each outcome_unknown_invalid_facts is well signed and well sealed (both verifiers take it, and its sealed_hash names its sealed part), but its sealed facts aren't a delegated task's: the recipient refuses it at open (malformed).
